Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a concise package (see attachments) and a short narrative below to get you started; Kim from Security is looped in for technical detail.

Key narrative (short form):
- Purpose: "Deployment borders" describes the logical and operational boundaries we maintain to prevent cross-customer access and to isolate control and data planes across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private offerings.
- Boundaries: Control plane (management/orchestration) is logically separated from data plane (inference requests, model KV caches). For Dedicated, control plane services are available over a dedicated management VLAN with strict ACLs; for Private (VPC/on-prem), customers control the management network and we run a customer-scoped control plane in their environment where required.
- Tenant fencing: Authentication + tenant ID binding at the API gateway, runtime token isolation, and TLS-encrypted in-flight KV cache segments. Default-deny networking between tenant compute instances; inter-tenant communication only via monitored egress proxies if explicitly configured.
- Egress and monitoring: Egress filtering at the tenant edge (customer VPC or dedicated egress proxies) plus centralized telemetry streams (anonymized/event-level) for anomaly detection.

Hi Sarah — adding the technical appendix and the SOC 2 mapping table notes below. See attached segmentation-matrix.xlsx and soc2-control-map.csv for the full mapping and example artifacts.

Technical appendix (high level, actionable bullets):
1) Control plane separation
   - Hosted: control plane runs in Redwood-managed control VPCs; management traffic to tenant endpoints is over mTLS connections on a dedicated management subnet with whitelist-only egress.
   - Dedicated: customers get isolated GPU pools; the control plane has per-customer management VLANs. Management APIs require client certs plus OAuth tokens; logging is forwarded to the customer's configured log sink when requested.
   - Private (VPC/on-prem): two deployment modes: (a) control-plane-in-customer (preferred for air-gapped) where management plane resides in their VPC/on-prem, (b) hybrid where a slim control channel to Redwood is allowed via a customer-managed VPN.

2) Data plane (inference request path)
   - KV cache segmentation: per-tenant cache buckets, enforced by runtime keyspace IDs and memcache/TCP ACLs.
   - Model execution nodes are pinned to tenant-specific pools for Dedicated; Private on-prem uses customer-owned GPU hosts.

3) Network controls and egress
   - Default-deny host-level firewall on all compute nodes; egress through managed proxies with allowlist-based destinations.
   - Egress inspection for telemetry/scanning is supported; packet captures for audits are produced upon request under a scoped process.

4) Cryptographic boundaries
   - KMS integration: For Hosted/Dedicated we offer per-customer KMS keys (multi-tenant but keys scoped); for Private on-prem, customers can bring their own KMS/HSM and we integrate via standard KMIP/Cloud KMS APIs.

5) Audit evidence and SOC 2 mapping notes
   - control_map: soc2-control-map.csv (maps controls to artifacts: firewall-rule-export, access-audit-log, diagram pages, config snapshots)
   - evidence generation: segmentation-matrix.xlsx contains rule indexes and sample ACL exports we can provide as CSVs; packet capture request process is described in the attachments.
